arms.result: REFUSED at BOTH widths -- NOT a memory refusal: pre-existing public-API defect
arms.defect: plan_phase_admission(policy='reject') refuses whenever the requested worker width exceeds the phase's job count (runtime_memory.py: requested>admissible where admissible=min(memory-fit, requested)); api.py:293-303 passes the unclamped width, so ANY scene with fewer tiles than 'workers' refuses at the public API ('requested 4 concurrent phase jobs but only 1 fit' despite the single 12,261,629,952 B reservation fitting the 50,891,986,534 B base with ~4x slack). Reproduced in-process against the pinned tree AND confirmed present on main (runtime_memory.py:948, api.py:235). The message text ('only 1 fit') is misleading in the under-fill case.
arms.disposition: documented + committed (ad53b56a); NOT fixed -- public-behavior change requires a user-approved arc (protocol -> impl -> review -> E2E). Candidate fix: clamp the production call to min(width, len(jobs)) or route under-fill to queue semantics; blast radius: turns a hard error into a run for tiles<workers scenes.

barrier_seam_verdict: The 362-371 s seam is execute_geometry_phase (walls/aspect construction). Measured flat across shapes (346.8 at 3x8, 370.9 at 12x2, 366.3 at 72 steps, 484.9 outlier at 2 steps) -> CPU-throughput-bound, not width- or serialization-bound; it already runs concurrent admission-planned children (C6-40) and the X02 twin removed its kernel slack. The serial corner does not exercise it (verbatim serial route). No further measured lever exists inside the frozen contracts: reducing the work is a numerical change (forbidden); overlapping phases would break the frozen phase-admission envelope (phases priced exclusive-resident) -- a user-amendment decision with a bounded ceiling (~export+compute stage, <= ~14% of the 12x2 chain). NO X04 candidate is recommended pre-amendment.
remaining_headroom: At 24 CPUs the accepted 12x2 chain (1483.9 s cold) splits: run 57.6% (engine-saturated, 8.50x vs serial), barrier 25.0% (CPU-bound geometry), export stage 16.0% (degree-12, ~97% efficient), walls 1.4%. Gains beyond ~1.2x require either more CPUs (not authorized), cross-phase pipelining (admission-model amendment), or arithmetic changes (forbidden). The corner matrix closes the coverage gap: all four goal corners measured with bitwise-clean numerics.
